title: pkg/bindings, pkg/api: send the manifest index subject to the server
body:
podman manifest annotate --index --subject and podman manifest add --artifact-subject both work locally but do nothing when you run them with --remote. The flags are there and the commands exit fine, the subject just never gets set.

The value never leaves the client. The bindings copy everything into ModifyOptions and AddArtifactOptions before sending the request and neither struct had a field for the subject, so it was dropped. The server had a problem of its own too… ManifestModify rebuilds ManifestAddArtifactOptions by hand and left out the embedded ManifestAnnotateOptions, so --os, --arch and --annotation were getting dropped there as well.

This adds the field to both structs with the json name the server expects, regenerates the setters with go generate, forwards the value from the tunnel, and passes the annotate options along in the handler. I dropped the bindings unit test and added two system tests in test/system/012-manifest.bats instead, one per flag, and neither is skipped on remote.

comments.body:
LGTM
@CodeWithAK28 Thanks!  I've added a release note to your description.  Please tweak it as you see fit.
Also please add relevant context as part of the commit message, not just in the PR description.

Thanks for the review. I removed the unit tests and added two system tests in test/system/012-manifest.bats instead, one for `manifest annotate --index --subject` and one for `manifest add --artifact-subject`. Neither is skipped on remote, so both run against podman-remote in CI now.

While writing the --artifact-subject test I found that flag was broken on remote too, but for a different reason … manifests.AddArtifactOptions had no field for it, and in ManifestModify the server was rebuilding ManifestAddArtifactOptions without the embedded ManifestAnnotateOptions. So I added the field, passed it through, and let the handler carry the annotate options over. That also stops --os, --arch and --annotation being dropped for artifact adds.

The context is in the commit message now and I updated the PR description too. Happy to split the artifact part into its own PR if you would prefer that. :)

@Luap99 the new --artifact-subject test found something else. podman --remote manifest add --artifact hangs forever….the upload goroutine in Modify never calls artifactWriterGroup.Done(), so the Wait() after the request never returns. It fails the same way on main, it was just never tested on remote.
Pushed the one line fix as a separate commit so the test can pass. #24788 has the same line but has not moved since last year, so I did not wait on it.
